Integrative Biology PhD
Successful completion of the Integrative Biology Ph.D. degree requires:
1. Completion of the required course work
BIO 511 Professional Communication (3 credits)
2 credits of BIO 525 (Graduate Student Seminar)
BIO 530 Biological Statistics (4 credits)
One course from Molecular & Cellular Biology offerings (3 or 4 credits)
One course from Organismal & Developmental Biology offerings (3 or 4 credits)
One course from Evolution & Ecology offerings (3 or 4 credits)
One course in a cross-disciplinary topic from outside of the Biology department (3 or 4 credits)
Completion of 34 credits of doctoral research (BIO 699)
Formation of a dissertation committee
After completion of course work, students must pass a written qualifying exam in their field of research
Oral defense of a research proposal
Approval of a written research proposal by all members of the dissertation committee
Oral defense of an original dissertation and approval of the dissertation by all members of the dissertation committee
Required Courses
BIO 511 - Graduate Seminar Credits: variable; 1.00 to 4.00
BIO 525 - Graduate Student Seminar Credits: 1 (must be taken twice)
BIO 530 - Biological Statistics Credits: 4
Molecular and Cellular Biology
Students must complete one course from this list.
BIO 501 - Genomics Credits: 4
BIO 508 - Microbial Genetics Credits: 3
BIO 527 - Molecular Biology Credits: 3
BIO 534 - Advanced Cell Biology Credits: 3
BIO 571 - Marine Microbiology Credits: 4
Organismal and Developmental Biology
Students must complete one course from this list.
BIO 511 - Graduate Seminar Credits: variable; 1.00 to 4.00 (Topics: Evolutionary Development, Ecological Development, Stress in Wildlife, Coral Reef Biology)
BIO 513 - Biology of Fishes Credits: 4
BIO 523 - Immunology Credits: 3
BIO 554 - Biology Of Sharks Credits: 3
Evolution and Ecology
Students must complete one course from this list.
BIO 502 - Community Ecology Credits: 3
BIO 511 - Graduate Seminar Credits: variable; 1.00 to 4.00
(Topics: Conservation Biology, Evolutionary Development, Ecological Development, Coral Reef Biology)
BIO 537 - Evolutionary Biology Credits: 3
BIO 545 - Biological Oceanography Credits: 4
BIO 571 - Marine Microbiology Credits: 4
